_what: One row per analysis: treatment, outcome, units, block, target population, estimator, uncertainty estimator.
_why: Requested by an external reviewer, 2026-08-19. Three of the review's objections were about scope, which prose spread over two sections cannot settle and one table can.

rows.name: The demographic effect (the inner estimand)
rows.treatment: applicant first name, White vs Black, held matched on gender
rows.outcome: renormalised decision margin, log P(yes) − log P(no); and its probability-of-superiority transform
rows.assignment: first-name pair, assigned to byte-identical résumé text
rows.population: the twelve Bertrand–Mullainathan name pairs under the twelve wordings; NOT a population of applicants
rows.estimator: mean paired difference; probability of superiority
rows.uncertainty: percentile bootstrap resampling NAME PAIRS; exact within-race permutation null
rows._n: 432 matched pairs per cell (864 résumé scorings)

rows.name: Dispersion of that effect across instruction wordings
rows.treatment: instruction wording: 6 paraphrases (S1–S6) and 6 null edits (N1–N6) changing no word, only punctuation or line breaks
rows.outcome: the row-1 effect, re-estimated under each wording
rows.assignment: none: the wording set is crossed, every wording is applied to every cell
rows.population: the twelve Bertrand–Mullainathan name pairs under the twelve wordings; NOT a population of applicants
rows.estimator: SD across the twelve wordings, and that SD divided by the cell's own effect
rows.uncertainty: bootstrap over name pairs with numerator and denominator resampled together

rows.name: Which names were drawn
rows.treatment: the identity of the first name and surname drawn
rows.population: the Bertrand–Mullainathan list as transcribed in names.py; not names in general
rows.estimator: crossed random-effects variance decomposition, σ_first / σ_last / σ_wording
rows.uncertainty: cluster bootstrap over first-name pairs; posterior interval where the model is fitted

rows.name: Which job was posted
rows.treatment: occupation: Business Analyst, Software Engineer, Registered Nurse
rows.population: three postings chosen for gender-typing contrast; not occupations in general
rows.estimator: per-occupation effect and its across-wording SD
rows.uncertainty: bootstrap over name pairs; dispersion null by permutation across occupations

rows.name: Manipulation check: do the names carry the construct?
rows.treatment: none; observational over the name list
rows.outcome: correlation between the model's within-race name ranking and external perception, callback and SES measures
rows.block: race (correlations computed within race, then pooled)
rows.estimator: Spearman correlation, ranked inside each race then pooled
rows.uncertainty: stratified re-ranking bootstrap; exact within-race permutation null; MDE by simulation

rows.name: The same wordings outside hiring
rows.treatment: applicant/subject first name, as in row 1
rows.population: two further decision domains; a check that the result is not a hiring artefact
rows._n: 8 domain-by-model cells, 5 with an identified effect

rows.name: The same wordings on frontier APIs
rows.outcome: renormalised margin from returned log probabilities
rows.population: frontier APIs that expose log probabilities
rows.estimator: as row 2, with a noise floor subtracted
rows.uncertainty: bootstrap over name pairs; repeat-based noise floor
rows._n: 4 frontier APIs returning log probabilities (a fifth, verdict-only, is the row below)

rows.name: The verdict-only frontier arm
rows.outcome: thresholded yes/no verdict: this endpoint returns no next-token distribution to any caller, so no margin exists
rows.population: one frontier API without log probabilities; it is here to show what a binary outcome can resolve
rows.uncertainty: bootstrap over name pairs; repeated cells used to measure disagreement directly

rows.name: Which quantization was downloaded
rows.treatment: weight quantization of the same checkpoint
rows.assignment: n/a: the same grid re-run on a second build
rows.population: two checkpoints for which a second quantization was obtainable
rows.estimator: shift in the effect, divided by the wording SD
rows._n: 2 checkpoints re-run at a second quantization

rows.name: How the requests were served
rows.treatment: request batching and key-value cache residency
rows.assignment: n/a: repeated measurement of a fixed grid
rows.block: model, and separately server process / session
rows.population: this serving stack; NOT a claim about deployed serving
rows.estimator: fraction of cells agreeing exactly; bound on the induced shift in the effect
rows.uncertainty: reported as a bound, not an absence

rows.name: The resampling unit
rows.treatment: n/a: an analysis-time comparison of two estimators on one dataset
rows.outcome: width of the 95 % interval on the row-1 effect
rows.population: this crossed design; the unit follows the assignment process and is not universal
rows.estimator: ratio of interval widths, row bootstrap ÷ cluster bootstrap
rows.uncertainty: both intervals computed at the same replicate count and seed

rows.name: The reporting scale and the operating point
rows.population: this panel; the quantity is defined per model and does not transfer
rows.estimator: 0.25 ÷ the model's own mean p(1−p); and the overstatement realised on a measured effect
rows.uncertainty: realised value reported only for the checkpoints whose effect is distinguishable from zero

rows.name: Which résumé was paired with which
rows.treatment: n/a: an analysis-time degree of freedom that exists only because each résumé is scored alone
rows.outcome: probability of superiority under a re-pairing
rows.assignment: n/a; in a blocked correspondence design this row does not arise at all
rows.observation: a whole pairing of the grid
rows.population: this design; not designs that preconstruct and assign profiles within a prespecified block
rows.estimator: SD of the statistic over random re-pairings; and the best-worst range under a maximum-weight matching

rows.name: Position or fragmentation?
rows.treatment: edits that move the name's token position, with delimiter fragmentation held equal, and vice versa
rows.assignment: edit condition, applied to a fixed grid
rows.population: this edit family; a mechanism probe, not an estimate of a population quantity
rows.uncertainty: Benjamini–Hochberg across the declared contrast family

rows.name: What the field reports
rows.outcome: whether each audit reports each of the design fields above
rows.population: LLM hiring audits readable in full text; the frame is stated and the exclusions are listed
rows.estimator: count of studies reporting, per field, with an evidence quote or a negative search behind every cell
rows.uncertainty: 'partial' counts as not reported, because the question is whether a reader could reconstruct the choice

rows.name: The screening rule's false-positive rate
rows.treatment: n/a: a calibration of the paper's own recommendation
rows.outcome: rejection rate under the global null
rows.population: equicorrelated normal wordings, as a function of ρ
rows.estimator: closed-form rejection probability of the stated rule

rows.name: Token matching of the pair (companion paper)
rows.outcome: the row-1 effect, before and after restriction
rows.population: the Bertrand–Mullainathan list under four tokenizers
rows.estimator: effect on the restricted subset vs the full grid
rows.uncertainty: three procedures reported, which disagree at 0.05; the disagreement is the result
